case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Department of Health & Rehabilitative Services v. M.B.
key_cases.holding: A child's out-of-court statements that satisfy section 90.803(23)'s reliability safeguards are admissible as substantive evidence in a dependency hearing even when they are inconsistent with the child's in-court testimony, and dependency itself is proved by a preponderance of the evidence.
key_cases.relevance: M.B. supplies the evidentiary basis on which a finding of abuse can rest and the reliability findings a court must make before crediting a child's report.
key_cases.quote: are admissible as substantive evidence in a dependency hearing once they have satisfied the stringent reliability safeguards established in section 90.803(23) and refined in our prior case law

key_cases.case_name: R.F. v. Florida Department of Children & Families
key_cases.holding: Proof that a parent sexually abused one child does not by itself establish that a sibling is dependent; the court must examine all the circumstances to decide whether the parent poses a substantial risk of imminent abuse or neglect to the other child.
key_cases.relevance: A substantiated finding as to one child cannot be mechanically extended to siblings; prospective abuse must be proved on the whole record.
key_cases.quote: While the commission of such an act may be highly relevant, it is not automatically dispositive of the issue of dependency.

key_cases.case_name: Padgett v. Department of Health & Rehabilitative Services
key_cases.holding: Parental rights may be involuntarily terminated only on clear and convincing proof that reunification poses a substantial risk of significant harm to the child and that termination is the least restrictive means of protecting the child, which ordinarily requires a good-faith agency effort to rehabilitate the parent and reunite the family; abuse of one child may supply grounds as to another child.
key_cases.relevance: Padgett fixes the evidentiary weight a Florida agency finding must ultimately carry if it is to support severance, disciplining what a substantiation can be used for downstream.
key_cases.quote: the state must show by clear and convincing evidence that reunification with the parent poses a substantial risk of significant harm to the child

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: Before a State may sever completely and irrevocably the rights of parents in their natural child, due process requires proof by at least clear and convincing evidence; New York's fair-preponderance standard was unconstitutional.
key_cases.relevance: Santosky is the federal floor that separates an administrative finding from the proof needed to sever parental rights.
key_cases.quote: due process requires that the State support its allegations by at least clear and convincing evidence
